label: First token is 2, p, or t (step 0)
explanation: Token-identity detector at the very first step: fires at t=0 whenever the first original token is 2, p, or t (precision 1.0 on dev). Magnitude is set by token: 2 gives the maximum activation (~0.077, about 66% of mass), t about 0.31x max, p about 0.22x max. A small residual (~0.6% of mass) fires at t=1 when the sequence starts r,2 (about 0.26x max). Never fires at t>=2, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase, and not on other tokens at t=0 or on 2/p/t at later positions.

issues: Minor: the label leaves out the small t=1 case (r then 2), which is about 0.6% of mass and about 1.1% of active steps. The explanation does cover it.

Checked and consistent: on test the predicate scores P=R=F1=mass recall=1.0, and misses finds 0 missed activations and 0 false positives. The t=0 clause alone gets P=1.0, R=0.989, F1=0.9945, mass recall 0.994. The r-then-2 clause is precise (P=1.0, 110 steps). Plain t=1 & in_tok==2 has precision 0.03, so the r context is required. On dev it never fires at t>=2, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase. The mass ratios fit the claimed magnitudes: 2 ~66%, t ~0.32x the max per step, p ~0.23x.
